_comment: Pre-registered hook-latency budget (road-to-credible-install Phase 1). Committed BEFORE the first optimization landed, per the roadmap's pre-registration discipline: the numbers below are the acceptance bar the precompile + single-process work is measured against, not a post-hoc fit. Consumed by the bench harness (scripts/bench_hook_latency) and its CI gate. Every budget carries an owner and a review date per the Phase-6 budget-ownership lint.

hardware_reference.ci: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner (the numbers the gate enforces)
hardware_reference.floor: 1 vCPU reference container (documented ceiling, not CI-enforced)

budgets_ms._posture_comment: A cap may only BLOCK where it sits outside its own metric's measured spread. Measured 2026-08-19 on ONE unchanged commit (release PR #1427 / main at the same hour): pre_tool_use p95 read 107, 152, 152 and 187 ms across four CI runs — a 45 ms swing eight minutes apart with no diff between them. The 150 cap sits INSIDE that 107-187 spread, so it decided the build on which runner the job landed rather than on this tree's cost, and it did so at release time roughly every third release. It is therefore ADVISORY (reported on every run, never fails a build) and NOT raised: raising a pre-registered number to buy headroom is the defect this file's own regression_gate comment warns about, and the 150 stays useful as the line the normalized instrument below is meant to replace. any_hook_event stays BLOCKING at 250 — that one sits above the whole observed band, so it still catches the pathology this budget was registered for (the 9.8.0 baseline was ~1.6 s p50) without reading load as regression. Enforcement lives in bench_hook_latency.ts::capsFor, which applies BOTH caps to pre_tool_use so the advisory downgrade does not drop that slot out of the blocking gate.

gate_remeasure._comment: --gate only, and only for a slot already over its tightest cap: re-measure and keep the MINIMUM p95. A load spike inside one 50-run sample moves p95 up and never down, so the minimum discards the spike rather than recording it. Bounded honestly — consecutive samples inside ONE job are correlated, so this removes a spike WITHIN a run and does not rescue a job on a runner that is slow for its whole lifetime; that case is what the advisory posture above covers. Costs nothing on the green path.

normalized.control: node -e 0, measured through the identical spawnSync harness in the same run
normalized._comment: The instrument the absolute caps cannot be: every slot reading is spawn + interpreter start + bundle load + concern work, and only the last term is ours while the first two scale with runner load. excess_ms = slot_p95 - control_p95 is therefore this tree's own cost, and it is the gating candidate rather than the ratio (whose noisy denominator moves a loaded runner toward GREEN — the wrong direction for a safety net to fail). Ships OBSERVE-ONLY on the same definition-before-bar rule per_turn_composite states for itself: no historical run recorded a control, so any bar set today would be invented rather than measured, which the evaluator-budgets contract forbids. Arming it is a CONFIG change once the nightly has published enough control-carrying runs — set p95_excess_ci from that data and observe_only to false; no code change is needed.
normalized._measured_limitation_2026_08_19: FIRST CI READING PARTLY FALSIFIES THE CONTROL AS DESIGNED, and it is recorded here so nobody arms this row believing a property that was not shown. Same commit, two environments: darwin local read slot 101 / control 45 / excess 56 ms; GitHub ubuntu read slot 151 / control 26 / excess 124 ms. The control went DOWN while the slot went UP, so the excess more than doubled rather than staying invariant. Cause: node -e 0 isolates interpreter startup only, while a dispatch additionally loads a ~1 MB bundle and runs the concern chain — and that bundle-load term is both dominant and the part that actually varies with runner conditions, so the control under-corrects. Consequence for arming: excess_ms is NOT portable across hardware classes and a bar set from a local reading would be wrong by ~2x. That is the same constraint the absolute budgets already carry (hardware_reference names CI as the gated environment), so it does not sink the approach — but the property that WOULD justify gating on excess, namely that it is more stable than the absolute across runs on the SAME runner class, is still UNMEASURED. Collect it from the nightly before setting p95_excess_ci; a single run cannot show stability. If the collected excess turns out no more stable than the absolute, the honest outcome is to say so and keep the row observe-only rather than arm a second flapping gate.
normalized._open_question: Whether the floor genuinely drifted is UNRESOLVED and this instrument is what will answer it. docs/hook-latency.json records the 2026-07-27 CI baseline at pre_tool_use p95 81 ms via bundle; the quiet-runner reading on 2026-08-19 was 107 ms, ~32% above it. The regression net cannot see that: max_regression_pct is 200, so 81 ms tolerates up to 243 ms. Absolute caps that flap plus a relative net that tolerates a tripling means neither instrument currently distinguishes a real 32% regression from a quiet runner — that gap, not the flapping alone, is what this block exists to close.

per_turn_composite._comment: D-1 of road-to-per-turn-hook-economy: the slot budgets above gate per EVENT, and a single tool call fires both pre_tool_use and post_tool_use with their full concern chains. A ten-tool-call turn therefore pays twenty dispatcher cold starts plus the prompt and stop slots while every individual slot stays green — the number the user experiences has no row. This row is that number. Registered by step 4.1; the CEILING is step 4.2 and is the maintainer's, so the row ships observe-only and CANNOT fail a build. Definition before bar, deliberately: two people computing two different composites would both call the row green.
per_turn_composite._aggregation_note: Documentation of the code, not an input to it: the bench reads tool_calls from this file but hardcodes the p50 aggregation and re-implements the formula, so editing `aggregation` or `definition` changes nothing. Kept because a row whose meaning lives only in a TS file is unreadable here; corrected from silence to a stated non-binding after the R2 review flagged both keys as unread.
per_turn_composite._observe_only_note: While observe_only is true the bench PRINTS the composite on every run, including the CI gate run, and never fails on it. Setting p50_ci to a number and observe_only to false is the whole of step 4.2 — no code change is needed to arm it. Do not arm it from a single run: the composite sums four slot measurements and multiplies two of them by tool_calls, so it accumulates runner variance faster than any single slot (risk 5), which is why the same absolute-cap-plus-pathology-net posture the slots use applies here too.

regression_gate._comment: Pathology net only — the ABSOLUTE budgets above are the binding gate for wall-clock. The original 20% window was falsified by measured GitHub-runner variance: two CI runs of IDENTICAL code measured p95 77-89 ms and 92-103 ms (+23% run-to-run, 2026-07-27, runs 30303438480 / round-2 tests.yml). Same rationale as the regression_pct 200 override on the evaluator timing budgets: a tight creep rule on shared-runner wall-clock flaps; sizes/counts keep tight windows, timings get absolute caps.

honest_null_consequence: If the budget is missed after precompile + single-process + lazy I/O, hooks ship default-off with an explicit opt-in flag and the measured numbers published under a 'known cost' heading. A resident-dispatcher daemon is NOT improvised as a rescue (council 2026-07-26).
